MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, Housing
  Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  December 9, 2025
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library
Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Ruesch at
5:00 p.m., on December 9, 2025, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by
5:00 p.m. on December 4, 2025, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. A copy was also posted at
the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive and Norman P. Murray
Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Vasquez
  Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum
  Mayor Ruesch

Absent:  Council Member Goodell

Staff Present:  Elaine Lister, City Manager
  Jerry Hill, Assistant City Manager
  John R. Harper, Interim City Attorney
  Ellis Chang, Director of Administrative Services
  Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk
  Renata Winter, Assistant City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Public Employee Annual Performance Evaluation- [Government Code § 54957(b)(1)] Titles:
  City Manager and Assistant City Manager

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:00 pm Mayor Ruesch recessed to Closed Session. At the hour of 6:02 pm Mayor
Ruesch reconvened the meeting with four Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

Interim City Attorney Harper stated the council met in closed session and discussed
performance evaluations but there is no reportable action.
City Council Minutes  1  December 9, 2025
 INVOCATION: Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Vasquez

PRESENTATIONS

P1. Animal Services Presentation

  Mayor Ruesch presented certificates of recognition.

P2. 2025 State of the City

  Received video presentation.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Kevin Liang, M.V.: A Sophomore at Santa Margarita Catholic High School and a member of the
Community of Character Committee, introduced this month's character trait – Caring.

Saundra Jacobs, M.V.: As a Santa Margarita Water District Board Member she shared the Water
District’s 2025 Accomplishments Report and announced some upcoming infrastructure tours that are
scheduled in the new year.

Michael Rotcher, M.V.: Recited a poem he had written.

Carlos Pianelli, M.V.: Thanked Mayor Ruesch for the job he has done during his first term and spoke
on President Trump’s policies.

Larry Gilbert, M.V.: Spoke on Consent Calendar item #16 and voiced his concerns and asked various
questions regarding the Stein Mart property.

Michael Schlesinger, M.V.: Criticized the City Council for failing to appoint Council Member Vasquez
to Mayor Pro Tem the last two years a disgrace and discriminatory. He asked the Council if they are
aware of the population of Mission Viejo is 19.6% Latino and Hispanic. He stated that Cynthia has
proven herself to be the best City Council Member because she is the fiscal conservative member of
the organization.

Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Asked that the City Council postpone their vote on item number 16 until all
information is received and questioned why this was on the Consent Calendar without council
discussion or public disclosure.

Stacy Holmes, M.V.: Encouraged the Council to appoint Council Member Vasquez to serve as Mayor
in 2026. Questioned the Council on not appointing her because she is not a Republican or they are
perhaps closet racists.

City Council Minutes  2  December 9, 2025
 Lynn Holmes, M.V.: Complimented the City on the Christmas lights all over the City. Spoke in favor
of Council Member Vasquez and criticized Mayor Ruesch.

Steve Nelson, M.V.: Stated he has been a volunteer helping JPL conduct engineering contests for
about 25 years now. He announced that Mission Viejo High School recently came in first place at the
Orange County JPL Invention Challenge and then they came in second place at the finals in
Pasadena. He encouraged the Council to recognize them at a future meeting.

Cathy Palmer, M.V.: Asked for an update on our progress towards the city’s Housing Element. Spoke
in favor of the appointment of Council Member Vasquez as Mayor in 2026.

Ron Moatamer, M.V.: Spoke on the construction of his home and the citations he has received which
he is going to protest. He stated that the project is moving forward. He commended the City on all the
wonderful work that has been done throughout the City.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Item #16 was removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.

Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, seconded by Mayor Ruesch, to approve the Consent
Calendar outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  Goodell

1.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of November 11, 2025, as presented.

2.  General Check Register Dated October 31, 2025, in the Amount of $1,273,262.67

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

3.  General Check Register Dated November 7, 2025, in the Amount of $2,957,720.71

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  General Check Register Dated November 14, 2025, in the Amount of $1,801,884.78

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  Golf Check Register Dated October 31, 2025, in the Amount of $85,933.94

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

City Council Minutes  3  December 9, 2025
 6.  Golf Check Register Dated November 7, 2025, in the Amount of $8,937.55

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

7.  Golf Check Register Dated November 14, 2025, in the Amount of $282,037.27

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

8.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for October 2025

  Received and filed.

9.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA) Treasurer’s
  Monthly Report for October 2025

  Received and filed.

10. Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly Report for
  October 2025

  Received and filed.

11. Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for October 2025

  Received and filed.

12. Fiscal Year 2024/25 Mission Viejo Housing Authority Annual Report

  Received and filed.

13. Crucero Park Play Area Rehabilitation (CIP 340) - Notice of Completion

  (1) Certified the completion of and accept the improvements for the subject project; (2) authorized
  the City Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (3) authorized the City Clerk to record Notice
  of Completion with the County of Orange and to release the Faithful Performance and Payment
  Bonds one year and thirty- five (35) days respectively, after the date of recordation of the Notice
  of Completion, contingent upon no claims or liens being filed with the City and (4) authorized the
  payment of the final retention of $46,455.55, thirty-five (35) days after the date of recordation of
  the Notice of Completion.

14. Highway Safety Improvement Program (HSIP) Enhanced Pedestrian Safety Improvements,
  Various Locations (CIP 24257)

  (1) Adopted Resolution 25-42 Amending the Fiscal Year 2025/2026 Budget for Costs Related to
  CIP 24257; and (2) awarded the construction contract for the subject project to Alfaro
  Communication Construction, Inc. (A25-38) in the amount of $294,694.00.

City Council Minutes  4  December 9, 2025
 15. Solid Waste and Recycling Consulting Services - State Diversion Compliance Consultant

  (1) Authorized the City Manager to execute a three-year contract and up to two additional one-
  year extensions with EcoNomics, Inc.(A25-39) for "State Diversion Compliance Consultant
  Services," and (2) authorize the issuance of a purchase order to EcoNomics, Inc. in an amount not
  to exceed $88,355 for calendar year 2026 services.

17. Data Center Virtualization Software Renewal
  Awarded a contract for Sierra Recreation Center Rehabilitation design services and preparation
  of construction drawings to Jones & Madhavan Architecture Engineering (A25-40) in an amount
  not to exceed $80,000.00.

18. Sierra Recreation Center Rehabilitation - (CIP 26340)

  Awarded a contract for Sierra Recreation Center Rehabilitation design services and preparation
  of construction drawings to Jones & Madhavan Architecture Engineering (A25-40) in an amount
  not to exceed $80,000.00.

19. Amending the City of Mission Viejo Salary Schedule and Authorized Position Schedule

  Adopted Resolution 25-44 Amending the City's Salary Schedule To Be Effective January 1, 2026,
  and Authorized Position Schedule To Be Effective January 3, 2026.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

16. Surplus Land Declaration for City-Owned Property Located at 25282 Marguerite Parkway,
  in the Mission Viejo Village Center, Pursuant to the Surplus Land Act (Government Code
  § 54220 et seq.).

Community Development Director Larry Longenecker presented the staff report.

Michael Schlesinger, M.V.: Criticized the City Council for not obtaining voter approval for the
purchase of the Stein Mart property and asked what they plan to do if the property is not sold. He
suggested erecting low-income housing to make the state happy and gives the ability to house
government employees like teachers to live here, or alternatively, you can use the property for that
performing arts center.

Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to (1) adopt
Resolution 25-43 Declaring the City-Owned Property Located at 25282 Marguerite Parkway as Surplus
Land and Finding That Such Declaration is Exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act
(CEQA), and (2) authorize the City Manager to circulate a Notice of Availability (NOA) and submit
appropriate documentation to the California Department of Housing and Community Development in
connection with the Resolution and the NOA process.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

City Council Minutes  5  December 9, 2025
 AYES:  Bucknum, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  Goodell

NEW BUSINESS

20. First Amendment to the Employment Agreement for City Manager, Elaine S. L. Lister

Human Resources Manager Monique Goetz presented the staff report.

Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, (1) receive oral
report and summary of recommendation of First Amendment to the City Manager Employment
Agreement with Elaine S. L. Lister per Government Code Section 54953(c)(3), and (2) adopt
Resolution 25-45 Approving the First Amendment to the Employment Agreement with Elaine S. L.
Lister as City Manager for the City of Mission Viejo, and (3) authorize the Mayor to execute the
agreement on behalf of the City.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  Goodell

21. First Amendment to the Employment Agreement for Assistant City Manager/Director of
  Public Services, Jerry M. Hill

Human Resources Manager Monique Goetz presented the staff report.

Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, (1) receive oral
report and summary of recommendation of First Amendment to the Assistant City Manager/Director
of Public Services Employment Agreement with Jerry Hill per Government Code Section 54953(c)(3),
and (2) adopt Resolution 25-46 Approving the First Amendment to the Employment Agreement with
Jerry Hill as Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services for the City of Mission Viejo, and (3)
authorize the Mayor to execute the agreement on behalf of the City.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  Goodell

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

22. Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG) Report

  Received written report.

City Council Minutes  6  December 9, 2025
 COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

23. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as
  presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public record.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley attended the Gifts and Goodies Holiday Boutique which was a huge success,
drawing visitors from across the county and she gave kudos to the Activities Committee. She also
attended Santa’s Arrival. She thanked city staff for the spectacular display of holiday Lights throughout
the City. She gave special thanks to Melanie and the Recreation Department for the great turnout at the
Winter Gala. She attended two ribbon cutting ceremonies supporting local commerce which remains a
priority. Council Member Kelley announced the upcoming Hanukkah Celebration on December 14 at
the Norman P. Murray Center and the Whoville-Themed Night Market on December 20. She gave
special acknowledgments to Mayor Ruesch commending him for his energetic and dedicated service
throughout the year, as well as city staff & volunteers recognizing them for their tireless efforts in
making Mission Viejo beautiful and vibrant. Lastly, she wished residents a Merry Christmas to our
Christian residents and a Happy Hanukkah to our Jewish community.

Council Member Vasquez

Council Member Vasquez attended the Hanky Hawk Trot at her daughter’s school which is always
fun. Her daughter had her first musical performance in Annie Junior. She attended the Thanksgiving
Meal Giveaway at Norman P. Community Center, which is one of her favorite things to do each year.
She also attended the Gifts and Goodies Boutique. Council Member Vasquez shared that her family
went to Maui over Thanksgiving week and they were interviewed by KTLA at the airport. She
attended the Stanta’ Arrival on November 30 and the holiday party hosted by Michelle Mitchell.
Tomorrow night is a school fundraiser her girl scout troop this Thursday has a service project at Ivy
Park by Home Depot. She said her oldest comes home from college this weekend which coincides
with our annual holiday baking weekend. She announced she will be attending the Jane Austin Ball
and shared that last year she won seven Jane Ausitn books which she has read all of them this past
year. She also announced the Girl Scout Cookie sales start next month. Lastly, she is looking forward
to having to spend time with her family for the remainder of the year.

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum attended the Gifts and Goodies Boutique and purchased a bracelet from one
of the vendors. It was great to see so many local crafters and support local businesses. She also
supported the Mission Viejo Daughters of the American Revolution and their fundraising efforts for
the obelisk project mentioned earlier and thanked the Mayor for highlighting that. They will be hosting
another cadence event at High Ground Coffee, and she encouraged everyone to stop by and support
them as they continue building awareness for America’s 250th birthday in 2026. She attended the
Mission Hospital Foundation’s annual gala, which was a wonderful New Orleans–themed event with
about 600 attendees and an impressive amount raised to support the hospital and the Sisters of St.

City Council Minutes  7  December 9, 2025
 Joseph. Mission Hospital is a vital part of the community, serving both a healthcare provider and major
economic driver. She reminded that holiday caroling will take place at the Potocki Center at 5:00 p.m.
on Saturday. Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum thanked the Rotary for organizing the turkey giveaway. Please
remember that Boy Scout Troop 787 is wrapping presents for donations—an easy and stress-free way
to support the troop. Finally, she thanked the public speaker that shared the information about Mission
Viejo High School’s second-place finishers. We appreciate the opportunity to recognize these students
and will follow up with the principal. That concludes my remarks.

Mayor Ruesch

Mayor Ruesch stated that to serve as a councilmember or mayor, the role requires significant
commitment—and your spouse or partner shares that responsibility. I want to sincerely thank my
partner, Debbie, for her unwavering support during my year as mayor. He begins with an important
reminder, especially during the holidays. While this season is joyful for many, others are struggling
with hopelessness and despair, including our veterans. If you see someone who may be struggling—a
friend, family member, or neighbor—reach out. It’s okay not to be okay, and a kind word can make a
life-changing difference. Resources are available on the City’s website, and I encourage everyone to
look out for one another. He announced On a lighter note, Santa and Mrs. Claus are in residence on
select days through December 21. Bring the kids—or be a kid yourself—and stop by to say hello.
Mayor Ruesch highlighted a few recent events. The Repair Café was a great success, helping residents
fix items that might otherwise end up in the trash—I hope we continue this program. He attended
presentations on the upcoming obelisk dedication, which will include a ceremony and marching band
on July 4th. He also visited Vocational Visions, an incredible organization that empowers individuals
with challenges to contribute meaningfully to our community. He expressed supporting and growing
our business community remains a priority. He recently met with the Taiwanese Irvine Chamber of
Commerce, and there is strong interest from investors looking beyond Irvine and considering Mission
Viejo. We will continue those discussions after the first of the year, which could bring exciting new
business opportunities to our city. Finally, he thanked the Council for the honor of serving as your
mayor. He hopes we’ve made Mission Viejo a little better, and he looks forward to supporting the
smooth transition to the next mayor.

CITY COUNCIL REORGANIZATION

24. Selection of Mayor and Mayor Pro Tem for 2026

Carlos Pianelli, M.V.: Strongly supports Cynthia Vasquez as the next mayor. He stated she is s a parent,
business owner, and an accomplished councilmember who serves with professionalism and grace. She
is also the first person of color elected to the Mission Viejo City Council and, despite her qualifications,
has never been given the opportunity to serve as mayor while others have done so multiple times. He
reminded the Council that tonight’s decision is about fairness and ethics, not tradition. He urged The
Council to do what is right and nominate Cynthia Vasquez as the next mayor.

Motion made by Mayor Ruesch, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to appoint Council Member
Bucknum to serve as Mayor in 2026

City Council Minutes  8  December 9, 2025
 On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Kelley, and Ruesch
NOES:  Vasquez
ABSENT:  Goodell

Council Member Vasquez addressed the City Council for the record the following statement:

Last year, I was passed over for MPT because the Council majority’s traditions & values shifted after
the 2024 election. I don’t believe they’ve changed. But now it seems acceptable to openly discriminate
against anyone who questions the status quo while representing their constituents. I don’t believe this
discrimination is solely based on intellectual differences - it is also rooted in race, power, and my
education and intellectual curiosity. This is what happened in Huntington Beach. Maya Angelou said,
“When someone shows you who they are, believe them the first time.” In the end, some people seek
these positions to feel important. But leadership is not about personal gain – it’s about fairness, service,
and upholding the values that guide us. You should all be embarrassed.

Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to appoint Council
Member Goodell to serve as Mayor Pro Tem in 2026.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Kelley, and Ruesch
NOES:  Vasquez
ABSENT:  Goodell

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 8:02 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Ruesch adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, January 13, 2026, at 5:00 pm

Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk
